items.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: I did the Vermont Jazz Summer Workshop, and that ... was Attila Zoller’s Jazz Workshop... I’d say that was a very big influence there. Especially meeting people in person.

ctx.x: Was there a significant live performance along the way that you got to see, or a number of them that heightened your interest in the music? Seeing some well known musicians perhaps?
Well I think what definitely helped a lot was doing the jazz workshops in the summer. Like in the summer of ‘94 and ’95 I did the Vermont Jazz Summer Workshop, and that © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

was Attila Zoller’s Jazz Workshop, and also I did Jazz in July Workshops, Billy Taylor’s workshop there. And meeting all those musicians and it was kind of a hands on experience, that really helped a lot. And of course they’d have the concert so you could work with them. I’d say that was a very big influence there. Especially meeting people in person. That was always very important to me. But I can’t think off hand of a particular concert.
